title: Heidi and Library (easy)
statementMd:
Your search for Heidi is over – you finally found her at a library, dressed up as a human. In fact, she has spent so much time there that she now runs the place! Her job is to buy books and keep them at the library so that people can borrow and read them. There are $n$ different books, numbered $1$ through $n$.

We will look at the library's operation during $n$ consecutive days. Heidi knows in advance that on the $i$-th day ($1 \le i \le n$) precisely one person will come to the library, request to borrow the book $a_i$, read it in a few hours, and return the book later on the same day.

Heidi desperately wants to please all her guests, so she will make sure to always have the book $a_i$ available in the library on the $i$-th day. During the night before the $i$-th day, she has the option of going to the bookstore (which operates at nights to avoid competition with the library) and buying any book for the price of 1 CHF. Of course, if she already has a book at the library, she does not need to buy it again. Initially, the library contains no books.

There is a problem, though. The capacity of the library is $k$ – this means that at any time, there can be at most $k$ books at the library. If buying a new book would cause Heidi to have more than $k$ books, she must first get rid of some book that she already has, in order to make room for the new book. If she later needs a book that she got rid of, she will need to buy that book again.

You are given $k$ and the sequence of requests for books $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$. What is the minimum cost (in CHF) of buying new books to satisfy all the requests?

## Input

The first line of input will contain two integers $n$ and $k$ ($1 \le n, k \le 80$). The second line will contain $n$ integers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ ($1 \le a_i \le n$) – the sequence of book requests.

## Output

On a single line print the minimum cost of buying books at the store so as to satisfy all requests.

## Note

In the first test case, Heidi is able to keep all books forever. Therefore, she only needs to buy the book $1$ before the first day and the book $2$ before the second day.

In the second test case, she can only keep one book at a time. Therefore she will need to buy new books on the first, second and fourth day.

In the third test case, before buying book $3$ on the third day, she must decide which of the books $1$ and $2$ she should get rid of. Of course, she should keep the book $1$, which will be requested on the fourth day.
statementZhMd:
你对 Heidi 的寻找终于结束了——你终于在一家图书馆找到了她，而且她还打扮成了人类。事实上，她在那里待了太长时间，以至于现在已经开始负责经营这家图书馆了！她的工作是购买书籍并将它们存放在图书馆中，以便人们借阅和阅读。这里有 $n$ 本不同的书，编号为 $1$ 到 $n$。

我们将考察图书馆连续 $n$ 天的运营情况。Heidi 提前知道，在第 $i$ 天（$1 \le i \le n$）恰好有一个人来到图书馆，请求借阅书籍 $a_i$，在几小时内读完，并于当天晚些时候归还书籍。

Heidi 非常希望让所有客人满意，因此她会确保在第 $i$ 天始终将书籍 $a_i$ 放在图书馆中。在第 $i$ 天之前的夜晚，她可以选择去书店（书店在夜间营业，以避免与图书馆竞争），并以 1 瑞士法郎的价格购买任意一本书。当然，如果图书馆中已经有这本书，她就不需要再次购买。最初，图书馆中没有任何书籍。

不过，这里存在一个问题。图书馆的容量为 $k$——这意味着在任何时刻，图书馆中最多只能有 $k$ 本书。如果购买一本新书会导致图书馆中的书籍数量超过 $k$，她必须先丢弃已经拥有的某本书，为新书腾出空间。如果之后又需要她丢弃的书，她就必须再次购买这本书。

给定 $k$ 和书籍请求序列 $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$，满足所有请求所需购买新书的最小费用（单位：瑞士法郎）是多少？

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $n$ 和 $k$（$1 \le n, k \le 80$）。第二行包含 $n$ 个整数 $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$（$1 \le a_i \le n$），表示书籍请求序列。

## 输出格式

在一行中输出为了满足所有请求而在书店购买书籍的最小费用。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中，Heidi 可以永远保留所有书籍。因此，她只需要在第一天之前购买书籍 $1$，并在第二天之前购买书籍 $2$。

在第二个测试用例中，她一次只能保留一本书。因此，她需要在第一天、第二天和第四天购买新书。

在第三个测试用例中，在第三天购买书籍 $3$ 之前，她必须决定应该丢弃书籍 $1$ 和 $2$ 中的哪一本。当然，她应该保留将在第四天被请求的书籍 $1$。
